title: PB Fintech put option buyers laughing all the way to the bank - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Put option traders of PB Fintech, particularly buyers, have plenty of reason to smile on Thursday, as the premiums surged dramatically following the sharp decline in the underlying asset’s value. The share price of PB Fintech on the NSE crashed 36 per cent or ₹679.10 to ₹1,207.20 (₹1,886.30).

Put options of strike between 1,120 and 1,700 were active; of them, the 1,400, 1,300 and 1,200 strikes were the most active as the stock crashed vertically after the initial 20 per cent circuit filter was removed.

The 1,500-strike of PB Fintech fell from ₹4 on August 24 to ₹0.3 on Wednesday. However, on Thursday, the premium jumped to ₹279.95. Premiums of other put options too jumped, since many of them are deep out-of-the money, not much interest were seen during the last few days. Only the 1,500-strike was active among deep OTM put options.

On the contrary, those who had bought call options of PB Fintech would have seen their value evaporating, as the premium nosedived. The premium of 1800-call slipped from ₹92.65.

Proposed caps on commissions, tighter expense-management limits and greater transparency could pressure new-business growth and margins, while the restriction on loan-linked insurance bundling may affect distribution volumes, said Vinit Bolinjkar, Head of Research, Ventura.

“PB Fintech and other broker-led platforms appear most vulnerable because their earnings are directly linked to commissions and take rates. LIC and SBI Life may be relatively better placed due to their stronger agency networks and lower distribution-cost intensity. However, the proposals remain at the consultation stage, with stakeholder comments invited until October 25, and final rules could be modified before implementation,” he added.
